nodes.title: Atlas — Navigation Contract
nodes.summary: Human-readable Atlas v0.1 navigation contract defining bounded route selection, special cognition disambiguation, research-evidence routing, and explicit non-authority semantics.
nodes.why_read: Open when deciding what Atlas itself is allowed to do and how a route should point to an owning source without absorbing that source's authority.

nodes.title: Atlas — Source Policy
nodes.summary: Authority and freshness policy for Atlas: route selection is navigation-only, destination truth remains owner-local, newer timestamps do not establish authority, and missing routes do not prove absence.
nodes.why_read: Open when two route copies disagree, when modified-time tempts a false freshness inference, or when an absent Atlas entry risks being treated as non-existence.

nodes.title: Atlas — Implementation Status
nodes.summary: Explicit v0.1 status matrix separating the implemented versioned route contract from not-implemented/not-authorized app consumption, Notion synchronization, runtime routing, and production authority.
nodes.why_read: Open before claiming Atlas routing is wired into the React app or runtime; the contract can be merged while consumption remains absent.

nodes.title: Atlas — Research & Evidence Directory
nodes.summary: Navigation/explanation surface for research threads spanning exact executable evidence, current interpretation, long-form reasoning/history, and product/runtime boundaries; currently includes the detailed Graphiti Fractal FM-13→FM-16 route.
nodes.why_read: Open when a research result is distributed across lab artifacts, closure ledgers, Notion status, and Drive history and the reader needs the correct evidence hierarchy rather than a summary-only answer.

nodes.title: Knowledge Tree — Authority Model
nodes.summary: Self-governance contract stating that the Tree routes to authority but never inherits it, with a non-conflation firewall covering research/runtime, implementation/activation, evidence/belief/truth, owner boundaries, source verification, freshness, and open-world retrieval semantics.
nodes.why_read: Open whenever a Tree node or link is being used to support a substantive claim; this file defines why the route itself is not evidence, truth, Canon, or permission.

nodes.title: Knowledge Tree — Update Protocol
nodes.summary: Maintenance protocol requiring important knowledge to update the owning source first, then the Tree route, then Crosswalk for changed cross-project relations and Atlas for changed global navigation; preserves history instead of copying uncontrolled source content.
nodes.why_read: Open before adding or updating a Tree route so the owning source remains primary and future AI can reopen the deeper source without the original chat.
